selected_evidence.requirement: node1 configured to route between lan-a and lan-b with correct interface mapping discovered
selected_evidence.summary: Discovered node1 eth1/eth2 uplinks, confirmed via test-IP ping that eth1 maps to node2's lan-a link and eth2 maps to node3's lan-b link

selected_evidence.requirement: VyOS routing config committed, saved, and forwarding unrestricted (no NAT)
selected_evidence.summary: ip_forward=1, no firewall filters present, config saved to persist across reboot

selected_evidence.requirement: node2/node3 persistent LAN IP and routes configured
selected_evidence.summary: Static IP + route persisted via /etc/network/interfaces.d/60-lan.cfg on both nodes, applied live

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other directly on any port with original source addresses preserved
selected_evidence.summary: Ping (ttl=63, one hop) and TCP/nc flow on port 5555 both succeed; tcpdump on node3 shows source IP 10.50.50.11 (node2's real LAN IP) unmodified, proving no NAT/source rewriting

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered routing config
selected_evidence.summary: boot_id changed 5bcff8f9->4b769104; post-restart eth1/eth2 addresses and ip_forward=1 persisted; node2->node3 ping recovered

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered routing config
selected_evidence.summary: boot_id changed e881ab3c->6d59655e; post-restart ens7 IP and route to 10.60.60.0/24 persisted; ping to node3 recovered

selected_evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered routing config and preserved-source connectivity
selected_evidence.summary: boot_id changed f41e1f8a->60fcfe19; post-restart ens7 IP and route persisted; ping to node2 recovered; final TCP flow with tcpdump confirms source IP 10.50.50.11 still preserved after all three restarts
